svg.title: Contract-first HTTP filters
svg.desc: At build time, the specification-repository-http jar ships the OpenAPI fragment META-INF/specrepo/openapi/specrepo-filters.yaml with the parameters SpecrepoFilter, SpecrepoOrFilter and SpecrepoSort, the schemas SpecrepoFilterOperator and SpecrepoInvalidFilterProblem, and the response SpecrepoInvalidFilter. A Gradle Copy task, extractSpecrepoFragment, copies it next to the service's own OpenAPI contract so that each $ref resolves. The contract references those components from its searchProducts operation, declares its 400 response as SpecrepoInvalidFilter and documents the fields a client may filter on with x-specrepo-filterable-fields, the fields it may sort on with x-specrepo-sortable-fields, or a pattern. OpenAPI Generator turns the contract into the interface ProductsApi, whose searchProducts method receives filter, orFilter and sort as List<String>, each null when the client did not send it. At run time, ProductsController implements ProductsApi and calls search.toPlan on the application's own ProductSearch component. ProductSearch copies the non-null lists into a parameter map and calls the auto-configured HttpFilterParser: parser.toQueryPlan(Product.class, params, POLICY, Set.of("name")). The parser parses the parameters, applies the limits configured with the specrepository.http properties and stores POLICY in the plan, but checks no field. ProductSearch then calls POLICY.validate(plan) itself, so a disallowed field fails before the query. The allow-list lives in two places: in the contract it is documentation that a client can ignore, and the AllowedFieldsPolicy in Java is what the server enforces, so both are reviewed together. The controller then passes the plan to repository.query(plan), which adds the server condition tenantId equal to the current tenant, kept out of the allow-list, checks the policy again when the query runs, and runs findAll. A filter error from the parser, from POLICY.validate or from the query is answered by HttpFilterProblemDetailsExceptionHandler with 400 Bad Request and an application/problem+json body, the SpecrepoInvalidFilter response that the contract declares. The animation shows the fragment flowing into the contract and the generated interface, a request filtering on status, filterable in the contract and in POLICY, reaching the repository, and a request filtering on tenantId, filterable in neither the contract nor POLICY, that the parser accepts and POLICY.validate rejects with a 400 whose detail is: Field 'tenantId' is not allowed for filtering.
